title: First-touch developer lab handbook — mini manifest
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, pragmatic handbook for the "first-touch" developer lab experience we run for new SDK users (internal and early external pilots). Goal: reduce drop-off in the first 15 minutes, surface predictable failure modes, and create a reproducible checklist for both engineers and solutions folks running the lab.

Audience:
- Engineers trying Redwood SDKs for the first time
- Developer advocates and SEs running a 20–30 minute lab
- Internal triage engineers who want reproducible repro steps

Guiding principles (short):
- Make the 1st request succeed by default: zero config that causes cryptic errors.
- Surface telemetry and SLOs quickly: show token costs, latency, and a simple trace.
- Offer two paths: "demo" (happy path) and "edge" (troubleshoot common failures).
- Keep it tiny: 6–8 steps, all runnable in a terminal or a single file editor.

Runbook (20–30 minute session)
1) Pre-lab prep (SE / host): ~5 min
   - Create sandbox API key with limited credits (notes: use ephemeral key policy).
   - Pre-provision small model route (gpt-small-ish) in hosted API or point to local dev stub.
   - Open the quickstart repo in codesandbox or participant's environment: GH link in linked_artifacts.

2) Welcome + context: 60–90s
   - What we'll do: make a request, inspect telemetry, add caching, simulate a failure and recover.
   - Quick diagram: client -> sdk -> route -> runtime -> model variant fallback.

3) Install and run: 3–5 min (the demo win)
   - Commands (node example):
     npm init -y
     npm i @redwood-inference/sdk
     export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-sandbox-XXXX
     node quickstart.js
   - quickstart.js: single-file that sends a short prompt and streams the response. (We include a ready file in the repo.)

4) Inspect results + telemetry: 4–6 min
   - Show console output: tokens, latency.
   - Open the Redwood Console route view (or local telemetry UI) and point out: per-request token breakdown, batching histogram, and a tiny trace that links the client invocation to the serving runtime.
   - Talk through what impacts cost vs latency (sequence length, presence of embeddings, batching).

5) Add a tiny improvement: enable prefix caching and re-run: 4 min
   - Swap in a config flag (sdk.config.cachePrefix = true) or environment var.
   - Re-run the same prompt a few times to show reduced per-token compute and faster tail latency.

6) Simulate and recover a failure: 4–6 min
   - Failure mode A: transient 5xx from runtime (simulate by toggling a flag in the dev stub). Demonstrate automatic fallback to a smaller model variant and show the SDK logs (level=debug) that record the decision.
   - Failure mode B: quota exceed -> client receives 429; follow the SDK docs to enable local request queuing with a 200ms backoff; re-run.

7) Closing + next steps (60–90s)
   - Where to find deeper docs: onboarding guides, SDK reference, telemetry troubleshooting page.
   - Offer an internal checklist we want participants to complete after the lab (see Post-lab tasks).

Minimal repo contents (what we should include in quickstart repo)
- README.md (short, < 200 words) with explicit ENV vars and expected output snippet
- quickstart.js / quickstart.py (single-file examples, streaming + non-streaming)
- small .env-template and instruct to copy to .env.local
- lab-checklist.md for participants with completion checkboxes
- telemetry-snapshot.json (example of what the console panel shows)

Lab-checklist (post-lab)
- [ ] Ran quickstart and saw a streaming response
- [ ] Opened Console route view and saw per-request tokens
- [ ] Enabled cache flag and verified a latency drop
- [ ] Triggered and observed fallback behavior
- [ ] Filed one usability bug if something confusing (link to GH issue template)

SDK ergonomics notes (issues to resolve in next sprint):
- Error messages: 429 and 5xx contain too little context for users (add route-id and model-variant in body).
- ENV vars: reduce number of required env vars to one (REDWOOD_SDK_KEY) and auto-discover region when possible.
- Quickstart output: add a friendly banner that prints route id, model variant, and token count in human-readable format.
- Local stub: make the dev stub accept a `--flaky` flag to simulate 5xx and latency jitter.

Open questions / discussion items:
- Should the lab require streaming by default? tradeoff: streaming surface is a stronger demo but increases flakiness for network-limited participants.
- Minimum supported Node/Python versions to document (current thought: Node >= 18, Python >= 3.10).
- Offer a "no-code" playground path for non-engineers (UI flow that mirrors the single-file quickstart).

Notes to implementers (todo backlog):
- [ ] Add lab-checklist.md to starter repo and wire GH issue template for post-lab feedback (owner: Ethan).
- [ ] Create ephemeral-key automation in Console (owner: Ava).
- [ ] Ship dev-stub `--flaky` and `--cache` toggles in sdk-dev-tools (owner: Liam).
- [ ] Draft error message format proposal and land in SDK errors RFC (owner: Priya).

Snippet: Expected quickstart console output (example)
---
> Request: "Summarize the key idea of Redwood Inference in two sentences"
Response (streamed): "Redwood Inference provides a unified runtime and developer experience for reliable, low-latency LLM serving..."
---
Telemetry summary: route: demo/small-v1 | tokens: prompt=18, completion=64 | latency=180ms | model-variant=small-quant | cache_hit=false

Relevant links (internal):
- Mini-lab templates (Confluence): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/DEVEXP/mini-lab-templates
- Quickstart repo (GH): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples/tree/quickstart-mini
- Telemetry troubleshooting page: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/OBS/telemetry-troubleshooting

Small appendix: participant troubleshooting cheats
- If npm install hangs: clear node_modules and try npm ci; if still failing, use codesandbox link.
- If streaming stalls: check proxy/firewall (switch to non-streaming fallback), demonstrate how to set SDK to chunked=false.
- If Console shows zero tokens: make sure env key maps to the sandbox route and not a management-only key (quick checklist in README).

This doc is intentionally compact — use as the single page you hand to an SE running a first-touch lab. Keep it under 1 page when printed.

Revision history:
- 2024-08-10 initial sketch (Priya)
- 2024-09-02 added failure simulation steps (Ethan)
- 2024-10-03 updated telemetry checklist and owners for backlog items (Priya)
